_comment: Template for config.json. config.json is gitignored, so this file is what keeps the schema in version control. Copy it to config.json and fill in the real values.
_excludedSenders_note: Every search gets -from:<each entry here> added. It is for blocking senders such as a crawler or feed you run yourself, which send dozens of mails a day and none worth a notification. It lives in this gitignored file rather than in a script, because a real mailbox address must not reach the public remote. An empty array or an unreadable file means nothing is excluded, and that direction only costs extra tokens and never loses mail.
_excludedLabels_note: Every search gets -label:<each entry here> added, to respect exclusion rules the user set up, usually labels a Gmail filter attaches as mail arrives. A label means the user has already decided about that kind of mail and wants no reminder, so the mail is not even fetched. The decision was made in advance on the rule, not by reading each mail, so a missing label does not mean the user has not seen that mail. What it saves is the tokens spent judging the same mails again every round. It is stronger than excludedSenders, because a label can sit on just one of a sender's mails while that sender's other mails still come in. For the same reason only the user may attach these labels, and the scheduled LLM must never infer on its own that something should be excluded. A label of several words is quoted automatically. An empty array or an unreadable file means nothing is excluded, and that direction only costs extra tokens and never loses mail.
_calendarIcsUrls_note: Google Calendar settings -> pick the calendar on the left -> Integrate calendar -> Secret address in iCal format. One URL covers one calendar, so each subscribed group calendar needs its own entry. The URL works like a password, since anyone holding it can read the whole calendar, so it lives only in this gitignored file. An empty array skips the calendar check, and events are then always treated as not on the calendar.
